text: A tiger's roar can be heard from about three kilometres away.
Pugs were bred in ancient China, well over a thousand years ago, as companions for royal families.
Axolotls, a kind of salamander, can regrow whole legs, and even parts of their heart and brain.
Super Mario first appeared in 1981 in a game called Donkey Kong, where he was called Jumpman.
The modern circus began in London in 1768, with a horse rider called Philip Astley.
Farfalle means butterflies, orecchiette means little ears, and linguine means little tongues.
Potatoes were the first vegetable grown in space, in 1995 on the space shuttle Columbia.
A teaspoon of a neutron star would weigh about a billion tonnes.
Light is so fast that it could go around the Earth about seven and a half times in one second.
Your heart beats about 100,000 times every day.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Antarctica is a desert. It is the driest, windiest and coldest continent on Earth.
A tiger's tongue is covered in tiny hooked spikes. They scrape meat off bones, and work like a comb when it washes.
A famous story says a pug named Pompey saved a Dutch prince in 1572 by barking when soldiers crept up on his tent.
Tardigrades, or water bears, are tiny animals that survived being taken into outer space with no protection.
The first home video game console, the Magnavox Odyssey, came out in 1972. It had no sound at all.
The word "circus" is Latin for "ring" or "circle".
Al dente means "to the tooth". It describes pasta cooked so it is still a little firm to bite.
Ramen noodles are yellow and springy because of a mineral salt added to the dough, called kansui.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the biggest volcano we know of, about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.
Sound travels more than four times faster in water than in air.
Babies are born with no kneecaps, only soft cartilage that hardens into bone as they grow.
The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.
The Sahara was once green, with lakes and grassland, until around 5,000 years ago.
White tigers are not a separate kind of tiger. A rare change in one gene stops them making their orange colour.
A dog's nose print is unique, just like a human fingerprint.
The mimic octopus can copy other sea creatures, like lionfish and sea snakes, to scare off enemies.
Pong was Atari's first game. Its creator, Allan Alcorn, was given it as a simple practice project.
Circus rings are almost always about 13 metres wide, the size that lets a horse gallop round while its rider stands on its back.
Spaghetti is a plural word. One single strand is a spaghetto.
It takes about ten litres of milk to make one kilogram of hard cheese.
A day on Mars is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
Count the seconds between a flash of lightning and the thunder, then divide by three, to get how far away it is in kilometres.
The hardest substance in your body is tooth enamel.
The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire: teaching there began over 900 years ago.
Papua New Guinea has about 840 languages, more than any other country.
The backs of a tiger's ears have white spots that look like eyes. Some scientists think they help tigers signal to each other, or make other animals feel watched.
Dogs can smell thousands of times better than people. Some are trained to sniff out lost people, and even certain illnesses.
A pistol shrimp snaps its claw so fast that a bubble forms and bursts with a bang loud enough to stun small fish.
The designer of Pac-Man said the shape came from a pizza with a slice missing.
The trapeze act was made famous in the 1850s by a Frenchman, Jules Léotard. The leotard is named after him.
Pesto comes from the Italian city of Genoa. Its name comes from a word meaning to pound, because it was made in a mortar.
Popcorn pops because a tiny drop of water inside each kernel turns to steam and bursts the shell.
Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is the furthest human-made object from Earth, over 20 billion kilometres away. A radio message takes about a day to reach it.
Your brain uses about a fifth of all the energy your body makes, even though it is only about two per cent of your weight.
The smallest bone in your body is in your ear. It is smaller than a grain of rice.
The Terracotta Army in China has about 8,000 clay soldiers, and no two faces seem to be the same.
Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Three kinds of tiger have died out in about the last hundred years: the Bali, Javan and Caspian tigers.
A border collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 different toys.
Bar-headed geese fly over the Himalayas, higher than 7,000 metres, where there is far less oxygen than at ground level.
The Minecraft creeper was an accident: its creator said he mixed up the height and width numbers while making a pig.
In 1859, Charles Blondin crossed Niagara Falls on a tightrope, and later did it blindfolded, on stilts, and carrying a man on his back.
Pasta was eaten in Italy long before tomatoes arrived there from the Americas in the 1500s.
Orange carrots were made popular by Dutch growers in the 1600s. Before that, many carrots were purple or yellow.
The Sun holds 99.8 per cent of all the mass in our solar system.
If you could stretch out the DNA from one of your cells, it would be about two metres long.
Red blood cells live for about four months, and your body makes about two million new ones every second.
Big Ben is not the clock or the tower. It is the nickname of the huge bell inside.
Russia has 11 time zones.
The Amur tiger, the biggest kind, can weigh more than 200 kilograms and lives in forests that get as cold as minus 30 degrees.
Greyhounds can run at about 70 kilometres an hour, as fast as a car driving through a town.
An Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year, a journey of more than 70,000 kilometres.
Pokémon was inspired by its creator Satoshi Tajiri's childhood hobby of collecting insects.
Cirque du Soleil began in 1984 in Quebec, with a group of street performers.
A real wheel of Parmesan weighs about 40 kilograms and takes at least a year to age.
Chillies feel hot because of a chemical called capsaicin. Birds cannot feel it, so they spread the seeds.
Venus is the hottest planet, at about 465 degrees Celsius, even hotter than Mercury, because its thick clouds trap heat.
The sky is blue because air scatters the blue part of sunlight much more than the red part.
Your brain cannot feel pain, even though it tells you about everything else that hurts.
The shortest war in history, in 1896, lasted less than an hour.
The Dead Sea is so salty that you float on top of it without trying.
A tiger can see in the dark roughly six times better than you, thanks to a mirror-like layer at the back of its eyes.
Dalmatian puppies are born pure white. Their spots appear when they are a few weeks old.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times a minute.
In 1979, a game called Adventure hid the first known "Easter egg": its programmer secretly put his name in a hidden room.
The first human cannonball act in Britain was in 1877, by a teenage performer called Zazel.
A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.
Saturn's moon Titan has rivers and lakes, but they are full of liquid methane, not water.
The Earth's core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.
Fingernails grow faster than toenails, by about three millimetres a month.
The Vikings sailed to North America around the year 1000, about 500 years before Columbus.
Tokyo is the biggest city in the world, with around 37 million people living in and around it.
Unlike most cats, tigers love water. They are strong swimmers and can swim for several kilometres.
A pug's flat face makes it harder for it to cool down, which is why pugs get hot so quickly. Dogs cool down mostly by panting.
Crows can recognise human faces, and remember who was kind or unkind to them for years.
In Super Mario Bros, the clouds and the bushes are the same drawing in different colours.
Tightrope walkers hold long poles because they make them steadier: the pole lowers their balance point.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
Diamond and the lead in a pencil are both made of carbon, just arranged in different ways.
Your skin is your body's biggest organ. An adult's covers about two square metres.
Machu Picchu, in Peru, was built by the Inca more than 500 years ago, high in the mountains.
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 centimetres taller in hot weather, because metal expands when it warms up.
A male lion and a female tiger can have a cub called a liger, which can grow bigger than either parent.
Dogs have a third eyelid, a thin one that sweeps sideways across the eye to keep it clean.
Dolphins give each other names: each one has its own whistle, and its friends call it back.
Sonic the Hedgehog was created in 1991 as a mascot for Sega, to take on Mario.
People have been juggling for thousands of years: there is an ancient Egyptian painting of jugglers that is about 4,000 years old.
The International Space Station circles the Earth about every 90 minutes, so astronauts see around 16 sunrises a day.
About half of the oxygen we breathe comes from tiny ocean plants called phytoplankton.
You blink about 15 to 20 times every minute.
The oldest known cave paintings, found in Indonesia, are more than 45,000 years old.
A tiger's stripes are on its skin too, not just its fur.
A group of pugs is called a grumble.
Honeybees tell each other where flowers are by dancing. The angle of the dance shows the direction.
Tetris was made in 1984 in the Soviet Union by Alexey Pajitnov. He named it after "tetra", the Greek word for four, and his love of tennis.
Joseph Grimaldi, born in 1778, became such a famous clown that clowns are still nicknamed "Joey" after him.
Comet tails always point away from the Sun, even when the comet is heading away from it.
Nearly all the internet between countries travels through cables lying on the sea floor.
The printing press was invented in Europe around 1440 by Johannes Gutenberg, and made books cheap enough for ordinary people.
Octopuses have blue blood, because they use copper, not iron, to carry oxygen around.
Many games draw 60 pictures every second. A cartoon film usually uses 24.
The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon, and about 400 times further away. That is why the Moon can just cover it in a total eclipse.
The first computer "bug" was a real moth, found stuck inside a computer at Harvard in 1947.
Starfish have no brain and no blood. They pump sea water around their bodies instead.
Speedrunners can finish Super Mario Bros in under five minutes by finding clever shortcuts.
At the centre of our galaxy is a giant black hole called Sagittarius A*, with about four million times the mass of the Sun.
Aerogel is a solid that is mostly air. It is so light that it is sometimes called "frozen smoke".
A mantis shrimp punches so fast that the water around its claw forms bubbles that burst with a shockwave.
The creator of Zelda, Shigeru Miyamoto, said the series was inspired by exploring woods and caves as a boy.
Neptune has the fastest winds of any planet we know, over 2,000 kilometres an hour.
Velcro was invented after a Swiss engineer noticed burrs stuck to his dog's fur.
A giant tortoise called Jonathan was born around 1832, before Queen Victoria became queen.
Uranus spins on its side, so each pole gets about 42 years of sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.
Post-it notes came from a glue that failed: it was too weak to hold things down properly.
A Greenland shark can live for hundreds of years, longer than any other animal with a backbone.
A light year is the distance light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion kilometres.
Lightning is several times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The "immortal jellyfish" can turn back into a baby when it is hurt or old, and start its life all over again.
Moonquakes shake the Moon, and they last much longer than earthquakes because the Moon is so dry and rigid.
A rainbow is really a full circle. From the ground you only see the top part.
A narwhal's long "horn" is really a tooth, and can grow up to three metres long.
Pluto has a giant heart-shaped plain of frozen nitrogen, called Tombaugh Regio.
An emperor penguin can dive deeper than 500 metres and hold its breath for over 20 minutes.
Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their whole head instead, up to about 270 degrees.
Male platypuses have a venomous spur on their back legs, and their fur glows green-blue under ultraviolet light.
A blue whale's tongue can weigh about as much as an elephant.
